featured_reviews.name: Yatri 5555
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Hanuman Mandir Bandra is truly one of the most peaceful and powerful spiritual places in Mumbai.

Located in the heart of Bandra, this temple has a very calming and positive vibe the moment you step inside. The energy here feels divine, and it’s a perfect place to take a break from the city’s hustle and find some inner peace.

The idol of Lord Hanuman is beautifully maintained, and the temple is always clean and well-organized. Whether you visit during regular days or on special occasions like Tuesdays or Hanuman Jayanti, the atmosphere is filled with devotion and positivity.

The surroundings are simple yet spiritual, making it a must-visit for anyone seeking blessings or just a peaceful moment in Bandra.

Overall, one of the best Hanuman temples in Mumbai—highly recommended for both devotees and anyone looking for a calm, spiritual experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Paradkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
'Hanuman Mandir' is located in Government colony, Bandra (E), Mumbai. It is very near from Chetana college. There are three temples inside this complex. In the left there is a temple of 'Lord Shiv, Parvati and Ganesh. In the right there is a temple of 'Shani' and in the middle there is a 'Hanuman temple'.
The surrounding area of the temple is maintained Very well, it is neat and clean. There are benches for devotees to sit and take blessings from god. Overall vibrations inside the temple area are very serene and peaceful.
If you're in Bandra (E), then must visit this 'Hanuman Temple'.

featured_reviews.review_text: I decided to visit a Hindu temple because the Hindu religion was the religion that I knew the least about and was interested in. This assignment gave me an opportunity to learn more about this religion and what their worship services and rituals were like. The temple that I went to was called BAPS Shri Swaminaryan Mandir and it was located in Lilburn. As soon as I walked in, I was amazed by the beautiful architectural design of this Temple. It seemed like it took a lot of hard work and dedication to make the place what it is now. While I was at the temple, I watched the Hindus perform an ancient Vedic ritual called the Abhishek, a ritual bathing to honor the murti of their God. Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha,

featured_reviews.name: Suresh Menon
featured_reviews.review_text:
This temple is located about 10 minutes walking distance from the Khar Road railway station.
The temple was established in 1960 by an ardent devotee. It is a small temple. It is very crowded on Tuesdays and Saturdays, days of the week that devotees consider special to Lord Hanuman.
The unique prefix 'ghanteshwar' can be attributed to the several thousand bells of varying shapes and sizes, that ecstatic devotees have donated to the temple, after fulfilment of their desires by the Lord.

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai shree Ram.
I went to Shree Ghanteshwar Hanuman After Hanuman Jayanti.
Every Tuesday and Saturday are especially  very busy, if you want to worship on these days, you have to wait almost one Or two hours in line. So many people come for darshan, Aarti, and to seek blessings
The temple premises are clean and the priests are humble and welcoming.
Visit once with your family 🛐🕉
Jai Bajrangbali 🕉🙌
